s.q: If a relation is defined on a small set and asks for the number of elements
s.n: Then for "minimum pairs to add to make it reflexive/symmetric/transitive/equivalence": add missing $(a,a)$, add reverses, then close under transitivity, in that order.

s.q: If it asks whether a relation is reflexive / symmetric / transitive / equivalence
s.n: For divisibility-type ($3x+\alpha y$ multiple of 7): reflexive gives $3+\alpha\equiv0$; then symmetry/transitivity follow. One counter-example is enough to say "not".

s.q: If it asks the domain of a composite function
s.n: Work from the outside in: e.g. $\log_3\log_5(7-\log_2(\cdot))$ needs $\log_5(\ldots)>0$ ⇒ $7-\log_2(\ldots)>1$.
